Get started

Source: vignettes/get-started.Rmd
get-started.Rmd

merchandise() selects logs from tree measurements and an ordered product table. It returns log dimensions, scaled quantities, tree totals, residual intervals, and recorded settings. The shipped tree inventories and product specifications are synthetic examples.

Tree and products

Default inputs use inches for diameter and feet for height.

## Select a shipped tree
tree <- example_trees %>%
  filter(tree == 5)
tree spcd species dbh ht model
5 202 Douglas-fir 20 100 F00FW2W202 
## Load the example specifications
specifications <- example_products(name = 'douglas_fir')
product lengths min_length max_length min_sed trim volume_unit
Large sawlog 32 NA NA 12 0.5 scribner
Medium sawlog 16 NA NA 10 0.5 scribner
Small sawlog 16 NA NA 6 0.5 scribner
Pulp 8 20 3 0.5 green_ton

volume_unit specifies each product’s measurement. The example prices use United States dollars (USD).

Logs and result tables 

## Select logs from the tree
result <- merchandise(dbh = tree$dbh,
                      ht = tree$ht,
                      model = tree$model,
                      species = tree$species,
                      id = tree$tree,
                      products = specifications,
                      currency = 'USD',
                      status = TRUE)
log product nominal_length sed_ib net_scale scale_unit
1 Large sawlog 32 14.017 230.000 board_foot
2 Medium sawlog 16 11.643 80.000 board_foot
3 Small sawlog 16 8.413 40.000 board_foot
4 Pulp 20 3.341 0.098 green_short_ton

logs holds the selected cuts. trees retains every input tree, including trees without logs. net_scale uses the accompanying scale_unit.

## Select tree totals
totals <- result$trees %>%
  select(id, log_count, log_net_cubic_ib, net_value, status)
id log_count log_net_cubic_ib net_value status
5 4 75.693 285.951 0 
## Draw the selected logs
plot(result)

residuals records stem intervals outside the logs. scales contains product measurements and any additional reports. defect_accounting records deductions, and values records priced quantities.

Inventory

ht_simulated supplies complete example heights. complete_heights() fills missing ht_observed values from retained measurements.

## Use the complete simulated heights and retain tree identifiers
trees <- example_trees_pnw %>%
  mutate(id = tree, ht = ht_simulated)
## Load the inventory product specifications
specifications <- example_products(name = 'pnw')
## Apply the product table to the inventory
result <- merchandise(dbh = trees$dbh,
                      ht = trees$ht,
                      species = trees$species,
                      id = trees$id,
                      products = specifications,
                      status = TRUE)
## Expand the inventory by species
stand <- stand_table(x = result,
                     trees = trees,
                     expansion = trees$expansion_factor,
                     by = 'species')
species merchandising_status trees_per_acre failed_trees_per_acre basal_area_ft2_per_acre logs_per_acre net_scale_board_foot_per_acre net_scale_green_short_ton_per_acre
Douglas-fir valid 226.4 0 375.053 623.6 76492 18.523
western hemlock valid 73.6 0 119.577 194.4 21908 5.944

Expansion factors are used as supplied. These example weights do not represent a sampling design. merchandising_status separates valid quantities, failed calculations, and inventory trees absent from the result.
